en: Paṭisambhidāmagga 1 Mahāvagga 1.9.
Discourse on the Path (Maggakathā)
In what sense is "maggā" (the worm) a "magga" (path)?
At the moment of the stream-entry path, right view is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong view in the sense of seeing;
it is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of co-nascent states; and it is [the path] for the exhaustion of the defilements.
It is both the path and the cause for purification through penetration; it is both the path and the cause for the resolution of the mind;
it is both the path and the cause for the cleansing of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction;
it is both the path and the cause for further penetration; it is both the path and the cause for the clear realization of the truths.
The path is both the way and the cause for establishing [the mind] in cessation.
In the sense of directing [the mind], right intention is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong intention;
it is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of co-nascent states; and it is both the path and the cause for the total exhaustion of the defilements.

And it is both the path and the cause for the purification of penetration and so forth; it is both the path and the cause for the resolve of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the cleansing of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction; it is both the path and the cause for further penetration;
it is both the path and the cause for the clear realization of the truths; and it is both the path and the cause for establishing [the mind] in cessation.
In the sense of embracing, right speech is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong speech; it is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of co-nascent states;
it is both the path and the cause for the exhaustion of the defilements; it is both the path and the cause for the purification of penetration and so forth;
it is both the path and the cause for the determination of the mind; it is the path for the cleansing of the mind.
It is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction; it is both the path and the cause for the penetration of what is higher;
it is both the path and the cause for the realization of the truths; it is both the path and the cause for establishing oneself in cessation.
In the sense of origination, right action is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong action, as well as for its co-nascent factors.
It is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of phenomena; it is both the path and the cause for the exhaustion of the defilements;
it is both the path and the cause for purification through penetration and so forth; it is both the path and the cause for the resolution of the mind;
it is both the path and the cause for the cleansing of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction; and for the penetration of what is higher.
It is both the path and the cause; it is both the path and the cause for the clear realization of the truths; it is both the path and the cause for establishing [the mind] in cessation.
In the sense of purification, right livelihood is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong livelihood ... pe ...
in the sense of exertion, right effort is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong effort ... pe ...
In the sense of establishing, right mindfulness is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong mindfulness … [and so on] … In the sense of non-distraction,
right concentration is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of wrong concentration;
it is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of co-nascent phenomena, and it is both the path and the cause for the total exhaustion of the defilements.
And it is both the path and the cause for the purification of penetration and so forth; it is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of the mind;
it is both the path and the cause for the cleansing of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction; it is both the path and the cause for further penetration;
it is both the path and the cause for the clear realization of the truths; and it is both the path and the cause for establishing [the mind] in cessation.
At the moment of the path of once-returning, right view in the sense of seeing ... pe ...

right concentration in the sense of non-distraction is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of the gross fetter of sensual lust, the fetter of ill will, the gross underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to ill will; and it is [the cause] of its co-nascent states.
It is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of phenomena; it is both the path and the cause for the exhaustion of the defilements;
it is both the path and the cause for purification beginning with penetration; it is both the path and the cause for the resolve of the mind;
it is both the path and the cause for the cleansing of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction; and for the penetration of what lies beyond.
It is both the path and the cause; it is both the path and the cause for the realization of the truths; it is both the path and the cause for establishing [the mind] in cessation.

At the moment of the non-returning path, right view in the sense of seeing … down to … right concentration in the sense of non-distraction, [is the abandoning] of the fetter of sensual lust and the fetter of aversion that are associated with the anusaya.
It is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion that accompany [the mind];
it is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of co-nascent phenomena; it is both the path and the cause for the exhaustion of the defilements;
it is both the path and the cause for the purification beginning with penetration; it is both the path and the cause for the resolution of the mind.

And it is both the path and the cause for the purification of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction; it is both the path and the cause for the penetration of what lies beyond;
it is both the path and the cause for the realization of the truths; it is both the path and the cause for establishing [the mind] in cessation.
At the moment of the path of Arahantship, right view in the sense of seeing … [and so on].

Right concentration, in the sense of non-distraction, is both the path and the cause for the abandoning of lust for the fine-material realm, lust for the immaterial realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance;

it is both the path and the cause for the supporting of co-nascent states; and it is both the path and the cause for the total exhaustion of the defilements. It is also the cause for the abandoning of the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to lust for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance.
It is both the path and the cause for the total exhaustion of the defilements.
And it is both the path and the cause for the purification of penetration and so forth; it is both the path and the cause for the stabilization of the mind;
it is both the path and the cause for the cleansing of the mind; it is both the path and the cause for the attainment of distinction; it is both the path and the cause for further penetration;
it is both the path and the cause for the clear realization of the truths; and it is both the path and the cause for establishing [the mind] in cessation.
The path of seeing is right view; the path of directing toward is right intention;
the path of embracing is right speech; the path of originating is right action; the path of purification is right livelihood; the path of exertion is right effort;
the path of establishing is right mindfulness; the path of non-distraction is right concentration.
The path of attending is the mindfulness enlightenment factor; the path of investigation is the investigation-of-phenomena enlightenment factor;
the path of exertion is the energy enlightenment factor; the path of pervasion is the rapture enlightenment factor; the path of tranquility is the tranquility enlightenment factor;
the path of non-distraction is the concentration enlightenment factor; the path of reflection is the equanimity enlightenment factor.

The path of unshakability by lack of faith is the power of faith; the path of unshakability by laziness is the power of energy; the path of unshakability by negligence is the power of mindfulness; the path of unshakability by restlessness is the power of concentration; the path of unshakability by ignorance is the power of wisdom.

The path of resolve is the faculty of faith; the path of exertion is the faculty of energy; the path of establishment is the faculty of mindfulness; the path of non-distraction is the faculty of concentration; the path of vision is the faculty of wisdom.
The faculties are the path in the sense of predominance; the powers are the path in the sense of unshakability;
the factors of enlightenment are the path in the sense of outlet; the path factors are the path in the sense of cause; the foundations of mindfulness are the path in the sense of establishment;

the right efforts are the path in the sense of exertion; the bases of psychic power are the path in the sense of success; the truths are the path in the sense of suchness; [the jhānas are the path] in the sense of non-distraction.
Calm is the path; insight in the sense of contemplation is the path; calm and insight in the sense of having a single flavor are the path;

the pair joined together in the sense of not overstepping one another is the path; purification of virtue in the sense of restraint is the path; purification of mind in the sense of non-distraction is the path;
purification of view in the sense of seeing is the path; liberation in the sense of being released is the path.

In the sense of penetration, clear knowledge (*vijjā*) is the path; in the sense of relinquishment, liberation (*vimutti*) is the path; in the sense of complete eradication, the knowledge of destruction (*khaye ñāṇa*) is the path.
In the sense of being the root, zeal (*chanda*) is the path; in the sense of origination, attention (*manasikāra*) is the path;

in the sense of convergence, contact (*phassa*) is the path; in the sense of meeting place, feeling (*vedanā*) is the path; in the sense of being foremost, concentration (*samādhi*) is the path; in the sense of predominance, mindfulness (*sati*) is the path.

The path is the path in the sense of being supreme; wisdom is the path in the sense of being transcendent; liberation is the path in the sense of being the core; and Nibbāna, which plunges into the deathless, is the path in the sense of being the ultimate goal.
The Discussion on the Path is finished.
